findings.evidence: Line 25 states the principle; line 27 cites the external source by name and scope but reproduces nothing from it.
findings.fix: Either reproduce representative findings from the 2023 research brief (e.g., the range of return-rate improvements observed across the fourteen systems, controls for confounds, statistical significance), or ground the principle in the pilot's own data by showing that the pilot's return-rate and avoidance improvements align with the pattern the research brief documents.
findings.location: lines 25 - 27, under "Why the Pilot Result Applies Systemwide"
findings.violation: The artifact advances the general principle that removing financial penalties for late returns predictably increases on-time returns and program participation (line 25). A target reader would not grant this causal principle without support. The artifact cites a 2023 Tri-County Library research brief reviewing fourteen systems (line 27) but supplies no evidence from that source, no findings from it, and no detail about the systems studied. The principle is named and asserted to be "documented" but the documentation itself is not carried in the artifact, only referenced externally.

findings.fix: Add an explicit conclusion-signalling phrase at the point the artifact states its central claim, for example "therefore" or "we recommend".
findings.location: the whole document, under its "Ending Overdue Fines Systemwide: A Recommendation" heading
findings.violation: No phrase from the conclusion-marker lexicon (therefore, thus, hence, it follows that, we recommend, this paper argues, I argue that, the conclusion is, in conclusion, we should, the case for) appears anywhere in the artifact, so a reader scanning rather than reading straight through has no signpost to where the conclusion is asserted.

findings.evidence: 10 of 14 sentences (0.71) carry at least one hedging term.
findings.fix: Remove the hedge from sentences whose claim the evidence actually supports, reserving qualification for the claims that genuinely need it.
findings.location: the whole document, under its "Ending Overdue Fines Systemwide: A Recommendation" heading
findings.violation: More than 0.35 of the artifact's sentences carry a term from the hedging lexicon (may, might, could, possibly, perhaps, arguably, somewhat, relatively, it seems, appears to, tends to, to a degree), spread across the whole document rather than concentrated where the evidence actually underdetermines the claim.

findings.evidence: Strong claims in lines 11, 17, 21. Qualifying language in lines 13 ("Arguably"), 25 and 27 ("in a somewhat qualified way"), 33 ("It might be that").
findings.fix: Qualify the central claim to match its grounds, or strengthen and show the grounds to match the claim. For instance, "the evidence from the pilot and parallel research supports a systemwide trial of eliminating overdue fines" is a qualified claim matching contested grounds. Alternatively, show the return-rate results, reproduce data from the 2023 research brief, and resolve the "It might be that" finance statement into a definite assertion; then the stronger claim becomes warranted.
findings.location: lines 11, 17, 21 for the claim strength; lines 13, 25, 27, 33 for the grounds
findings.violation: The central claim is asserted with high modal force: the change is "plainly the better path" (line 11), "the stronger choice" (line 17), and "removes every overdue-related charge permanently, for every item the consortium owns, without qualification" (line 21). But the grounds supporting this claim are heavily hedged. The avoidance survey is introduced with "Arguably" (line 13). The causal principle is stated as true "in a somewhat qualified way" twice (lines 25 and 27). The finance data is framed as "It might be that" (line 33). The return-rate results are mentioned but never shown. A reader acting on the unqualified central recommendation has no signal that the evidence that supports it is contested, tentative, or incomplete.

findings.evidence: Line 17 specifies the ask; line 19 dissolves it into "making things better for patrons going forward, in whatever way the consortium finds workable"; line 21 restates the specific ask.
findings.fix: Remove or rewrite line 19 so that all restatements of the recommendation align on the specific policy (eliminate overdue fines) or the goal it serves (reduce patron avoidance due to fine anxiety). Do not alternate between specific policy and vague aspirational restatement.
findings.violation: The artifact states its recommendation crisply in line 17 ("systemwide end to overdue fines across all ten consortium branches, effective at the start of the next fiscal year"), then restates it in line 19 as a vaguer aspiration ("making things better for patrons going forward, in whatever way the consortium finds workable"), then re-specifies it in line 21 ("removes every overdue-related charge permanently, for every item the consortium owns, without qualification"). Line 19's version is so general that a reader cannot disagree with it or tell whether the consortium is being asked to eliminate fines or to achieve the goal of better patron outcomes through unspecified means. A reader who reads only the middle statement sees a vague aspiration, not a specific ask.

findings.evidence: Line 17 refers to "return-rate... results" without showing them. Line 25 refers to the same results without specifying them. Line 33 hedges the finance data with "It might be that."
findings.fix: Specify the return-rate result: what percentage improvement, over what time period, in what metric (circulation, on-time returns, number of items returned). Rewrite line 33 to state the finance fact definitively (remove the "It might be that") or drop it if it is not known.
findings.location: lines 13, 17, 33, distributed across "What the Pilot Showed" and "Addressing the Revenue Concern"
findings.violation: The central claim rests on pilot results: return-rate improvements and a drop in avoidance. Line 13 specifies the avoidance-survey result (20% to 3% self-reported avoidance). But line 17 refers to "return-rate and avoidance-survey results above" without ever specifying what the return-rate results were. The artifact mentions these results support the conclusion and invokes them again in line 25 ("the pilot's return-rate and avoidance-survey results, taken together") but never states what the return rates were or how much they improved. A reader is asked to trust results that are mentioned but not shown. Additionally, the finance data in line 33 is framed as contingent ("It might be that consortium finance records show...") rather than asserted, leaving its status ambiguous.

findings.evidence: Objections raised and addressed: revenue shortfall (lines 29 - 33). Objections the pilot's limited scope leaves open but not raised: generalization to all ten branches, representativeness of the four branches, operational challenges.
findings.fix: Add a section acknowledging the scope of the pilot and naming conditions under which the result might not generalize or the implementation might encounter obstacles. For instance: "The pilot spanned four branches and one year. The result may not hold if the other six branches have different patron demographics or if larger branches face different operational constraints. A phased rollout could test this before committing to a systemwide change." Then address each condition you name.
findings.location: lines 29 - 33, the "Addressing the Revenue Concern" section; and by absence from lines 3 - 27
findings.violation: The artifact raises and addresses one foreseeable objection: the worry that eliminating fines will leave a funding shortfall for materials replacement. But the artifact does not raise other conditions its own grounds leave open. The pilot was limited to four branches over one year. The artifact does not name or address whether the pilot results will generalize to all ten branches, whether the pilot branches were representative of the consortium's broader patron base, whether removing fines at large branches will have the same effect as at the four pilot sites, or what operational or logistical challenges might attend a systemwide rollout. The scope of the pilot (four branches, twelve months) opens these questions; the artifact leaves them unraised and unaddressed.

findings.evidence: Line 25 says the relationship is "the reason" the pilot supports the systemwide claim, implying a warrant. Lines 25 - 27 cite research on other systems. But neither lines nor surrounding passages state the warrant as a general principle.
findings.fix: Add a sentence making the warrant explicit: for example, "When a pilot program demonstrates that eliminating overdue fines reduces patron avoidance and improves return rates, and that relationship has been documented in other library systems that implemented the same policy, the results justify implementing the change systemwide." State the principle once, plainly, so that a reader can see why this evidence bears on this conclusion.
findings.location: lines 25 - 27, under "Why the Pilot Result Applies Systemwide"
findings.violation: The warrant - the general principle that licenses moving from the pilot results to a systemwide recommendation - is not made explicit. Line 25 states that the causal relationship is "the reason the pilot's return-rate and avoidance-survey results, taken together, support ending fines for the whole consortium rather than only the pilot branches." This implies the warrant but does not state it. The implicit warrant appears to be: "If a four-branch pilot demonstrates a policy change improves returns and reduces avoidance, and that relationship is documented in research on other systems, the change should be implemented systemwide." But a reader cannot locate where the artifact states this principle. A skeptical reader would ask, "Why should the pilot results apply to the other six branches?" and the explicit warrant supplies the answer.
